panel.stale: The last check failed, so the list may be out of date: {message}

check_interval.description: How often to look for updates. Set to 0 to check only at startup, on request (right click on the widget, the refresh button, IPC) and after packages change.
check_interval.label: Check interval (minutes)

elevation.description: How the upgrade in the terminal gets root privileges. Auto picks the first of sudo, doas and pkexec found on PATH.
elevation.label: Run the upgrade with

hide_when_updated.description: Hide the widget while there is nothing to update. It still shows up when a check fails.
hide_when_updated.label: Hide when up to date

ignored_packages.description: Packages left out of the count and the notifications. Shell-style wildcards work, e.g. linux*. xbps-install -Su still upgrades them; use xbps-pkgdb -m hold to really keep a package back.
ignored_packages.label: Ignored packages

notify.description: Show a notification when updates appear that were not announced before. While announced updates are still pending, newer ones are announced at most every 6 hours.
notify.label: Notify about new updates

notify_threshold.description: Only notify once at least this many updates are pending.
notify_threshold.label: Minimum updates for a notification

sync_repos.description: Download the current repository index into memory on every check (xbps-install -M, no root needed). When off, only the local cache is read, which is as fresh as the last xbps-install -S run as root.
sync_repos.label: Fetch a fresh repository index

update_command.description: Replaces the built-in command (e.g. sudo xbps-install -Su). Runs with sh in a terminal. Leave empty for the default.
update_command.label: Custom upgrade command

status.unsupported: xbps-install was not found. This plugin only works on Void Linux.

terminal.close: Press Enter to close this window…
terminal.failed: ✘ The upgrade did not finish. See the output above.
terminal.title: XBPS system upgrade
